View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; getAddPaxOfferId/getAddPaxResponceID available. Collection variables reset before starting (SPEC.md §6.1).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (send ResponseId/selectedOfferId = AddPassenger's IDs) -> capture resp.offerId/resp.responseId -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId).
Expected Result
GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a non-empty offerId/responseId; the collection variables getSeatMapOfferId and getSeatMapResponceID (note the collection's own "Responce" spelling) are populated from these; Book accepts them and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR without needing AddPassenger's IDs re-sent -- this is a behavior change from before 2026-08-10, when GetSeatMap set no variables at all and Book still read AddPassenger's IDs.
Actual Result
Confirmed. GetSeatMap returned non-empty offerId/responseId (responseId different from AddPassenger's, offerId a re-issued value); Book accepted them and created a real PNR. FlyAdeal returns an empty bookingToken and an empty gdsPNR (only pnr is set) and no ticket - the booking stays unticketed ("Booked"); Retrieve by pnr alone works. The Postman collection-variable assignment is script-side and not observable over raw HTTP; the field mapping it relies on (resp.offerId/resp.responseId) was verified instead.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Hold completed; pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken available and not yet expired (holdExpirationDate in the future).
Steps
  1. Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> SeatAfterHold (POST api/v2/SeatMap/SeatAfterHold with supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName) -> record the raw status code and full response body verbatim.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design -- no expected shape exists anywhere in SPEC.md or the collection (§2.7a). This case's purpose is to establish ground truth: does it return 200 with a seat-map-like payload to choose from, does it require a follow-up call, or does it error demanding fields not shown in the saved example? Record exactly what happens; do not force-fit the result into an assumed shape.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-03, 10th confirmed occurrence overall; first on FlyAdeal). Ground truth: SeatAfterHold rejects FlyAdeal outright at supplier level before reading any field (the same 409 as for GulfAir, whose message names the supplier). The endpoint therefore has no usable contract for this supplier, and FlyAdeal cannot even reach it because Hold itself is unsupported (canBeHeld was false on every one of the 55 offers). A live Held pnr could not be obtained, so only the fabricated-identity probe was possible.

Expected: A full seat map for exactly the flight in the offer
Actual: Confirmed — once the fare bundle is supplied the seat map is complete and matches the offer. The bundle requirement is not in the specification and is proposed as an update

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; getAddPaxOfferId/getAddPaxResponceID available.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (send ResponseId/selectedOfferId = AddPassenger's IDs) -> inspect the raw response.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: HTTP 200; supplier, flightSegments, passengersDetails, seatMapDetails all present and non-null; seatMapDetails has at least one key; every segmentRefId key in seatMapDetails also appears in flightSegments and in the offer's segments from FareConfirm/AddPassenger (no orphan/missing segments in either direction).
Actual Result
Confirmed once the bundle choice is supplied. The seat map returned 200 with all four blocks; the single segment key (RjN_IDMwM34gfn5KRU...) is identical in seatMapDetails, flightSegments and FareConfirm (no orphan segment either way). NEW FACT: the documented 4-field body is rejected for FlyAdeal with 400 "selectedBundles list is null or empty" - GetSeatMap needs the chosen bundle per journey for this supplier (see SPEC proposal). The 400 is a clean structured validation error, so it is recorded as a contract gap, not a defect.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; a cellCode/cellId recorded for an AvailablePaid cell; the pnr's bookingStatus/ticketStatus (per Retrieve) confirmed not yet ticketed before this check is made.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats) -> Retrieve immediately afterward, with no ticketing action taken in between -> inspect bookingStatus/ticketStatus alongside the seat-related fields.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: the immediate post-Book Retrieve already shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeatsAmount populated with the selected seat, while bookingStatus/ticketStatus still reads as un-ticketed/un-issued (e.g. Booked, not Ticketed). This confirms the seat is attached to the reservation at Book time and does not depend on a later payment/ticketing step existing or completing. If bookingStatus already reads as ticketed/paid immediately post-Book with no intervening action taken, record that as a finding rather than assuming the AC's ordering holds.
Actual Result
The seat is attached at Book time: Retrieve, taken right after Book with nothing in between, shows the seat, its price and totalSelectedSeatsAmount, while bookingStatus is "Booked" and tickets is empty. The reservation therefore carries the seat before any ticketing/payment, and FlyAdeal never reaches a ticketed state through this API. (paxTotalSeatAmount in that Retrieve is 21.74, not 25 - BUG-18, counted under the flow case.)

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer; a specific AvailablePaid cell identified in the response.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> record cellDetails.cellID (capital ID) for a chosen AvailablePaid cell, plus its cellCode -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellCode and cellId=<the recorded cellID value>).
Expected Result
Book accepts the token despite the field-name casing difference between the response (cellID) and the request (cellId) and attaches the correct seat, echoed back in the response's passengersSelectedSeats/selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats.
Actual Result
Accepted. The request sent the response's cellID value verbatim under the lowercase-d field name cellId; Book returned 200, attached seat 18C and echoed it at three places (top-level passengersSelectedSeats, selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats, priceDetails.totalSelectedSeats). The casing difference is cosmetic (case-insensitive JSON binding).
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04 - Validate a cellID obtained from one offer's GetSeatMap response is rejected when submitted in Book for a different offer.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm a seat code taken from one flight offer is refused when used on a different offer
Request: Opened seat maps for two separate offers of the same flight, then booked on the second offer with seat 19C but using the seat code copied from the first offer's seat 19C
Response: The booking was accepted: reference TF6H6B, but no seat was attached and no seat charge was made
Expected: The booking should have been refused straight away, because the seat code belongs to another offer
Actual: BUG-07, 16th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the foreign seat code was not rejected; a real booking was created and the requested seat was silently dropped without any error
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Book 200 in 2.1s; pnr TF6H6B; passengersSelectedSeats {}; totalSelectedSeatsAmount null; variant 1: 409

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two independent, completed Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chains (Offer A and Offer B) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, record cellID_A. Chain B: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, obtain getSeatMapResponceID_B/getSeatMapOfferId_B. Book using Chain B's ResponseId/selectedOfferId but passengersSelectedSeats.cellId=cellID_A.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9), since cellID appears (per its base64-decoded contents) to embed the originating ResponseId/OfferId/passenger-ref metadata and is presumably bound to the offer it was issued for.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-07, 16th confirmed occurrence overall; first on FlyAdeal). With the same cellCode, a cellId taken from another offer is not rejected: Book ran to the supplier, created a real booking and silently dropped the seat (passengersSelectedSeats {}, no seat fee) instead of returning an error. The first variant is rejected only because the code does not match the cellId (cell-level check), which proves FlyAdeal checks code-vs-id but not offer-vs-id.
TC-BOOK-VAL-06 - Validate Book's behavior when passengersSelectedSeats.cellCode does not match the cell that cellId actually encodes.PASS

Response: Refused with a clear message that the two do not match

Actual: Resolved: the airline rejects a mismatch; nothing is booked

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; a valid cellCode/cellId pair recorded for one cell, plus a second cellCode value from a different cell.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (record cellCode="12E"/cellId for that cell, and note a different cell's cellCode, e.g. "14C") -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellCode="14C" but cellId = the "12E" token).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether the API trusts cellId alone (ignoring/overwriting the mismatched cellCode), rejects the request outright, or books the wrong seat under the wrong displayed code. All three are plausible given cellId is described as the metadata-bearing field and cellCode as a display label.
Actual Result
Resolved: FlyAdeal rejects the mismatch outright with a specific message, before creating any booking. It does not trust one field over the other (unlike GulfAir, which ignores the cellId and books the cellCode).

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger and GetSeatMap completed; two distinct AvailablePaid cellCode/cellId pairs recorded (cell A and cell B).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (record cell A and cell B) -> construct a Book request with passengersSelectedSeats=cell A -> before sending, replace passengersSelectedSeats with cell B -> send the single Book request (cell A is never actually transmitted).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds and reflects cell B only -- passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats show cell B's cellCode/price; cell A does not appear anywhere in the response, and cell A's availability (per a follow-up GetSeatMap, if re-queryable) is unaffected by the abandoned selection.
Actual Result
The single Book call carried 24D and the response reflects only 24D at every location (25 SAR); 24C is untouched and still AvailablePaid on the follow-up seat map while 24D turned Occupied. This is a client-side substitution, so the API sees one selection only - the case verifies nothing was cached or leaked from the abandoned choice.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell's cellCharacteristics[], pair padisCode with description -> check each pair against a maintained reference mapping (e.g. A=Aisle, W=Window, E=Exit seat, per the QC checklist's simplified mapping) -- note SPEC.md §2.7/§8.3 itself has observed a wider code set (CH, _8, _9, _14, K, LS, OW, RS, V, FC, Unknown) not covered by the checklist's simplified 5-code table.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: for every padisCode value observed, description must not contradict the code's known meaning per the now-sourced canonical reference table. Codes still outside that table should be rare -- log any such pairing rather than asserting pass/fail.
Actual Result
0 contradictions. Every real code carries exactly the reference wording (L = Leg space seat, K = Bulkhead seat, W = Window seat, A = Aisle seat, I = Seat suitable for adult with an infant, IE = Seat not suitable for child, _1M = Seat with movie view). FE ("Female designated seat") is not in the reference table and is logged. "Unknown" is used for FlyAdeal's own zone/wing/boarding attributes. Separate concern recorded under TC-SEATMAP-VAL-07: code K (bulkhead) is attached to 8366 of 8366 seats.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-06 - Verify every Aisle-category cell has column=null and cellDetails=null, and every Seat-category cell has both populated.PASS

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with at least one Aisle-category cell present.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell, branch on cellCategory -> if Aisle, assert column and cellDetails; if Seat, assert column and cellDetails.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: cellCategory=Aisle implies column is null AND cellDetails is null; cellCategory=Seat implies column is non-null AND cellDetails is a populated object (per TC-SEATMAP-REG-02's field list). No cell violates this partition.
Actual Result
0 violations: all 1395 Aisle cells have column null and cellDetails null; all 8366 Seat cells have a letter column and a populated cellDetails object.

Expected: The tags should agree with the seat position and description
Actual: New defect (BUG-23) — the bulkhead tag is on all seats, although the seat descriptions name a bulkhead only for the front row
Status: FAIL

Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every Seat-category cell, read cellCharacteristics[].padisCode -> classify each cell as window/aisle/extra-legroom/other using the reference table -> spot-check against the cell's own column position (e.g. the outermost column of a zone should carry a window-adjacent code) and description text.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: for codes present in the now-sourced canonical reference table (NDC_Integration/Resources/SeatResources/PadisSeatCharacteristic.md), the derived classification must not contradict column position or description text. Codes outside that table are logged, not failed.
Actual Result
Window and aisle are correct on every seat. NEW DEFECT: padisCode K ("Bulkhead seat") is attached to EVERY seat (8366 of 8366), while the cell's own description names a bulkhead on only 8 of them (the first-row seats). A customer-facing "bulkhead" filter would therefore select the whole cabin. Filed as BUG-23.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-08 - Verify seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is populated (non-null) for every AvailablePaid cell and null/absent for every Blocked or Occupied cell.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm only bookable seats carry a price and unavailable seats carry none
Request: Grouped all 8366 seats by availability and looked at their prices
Response: Every bookable seat is priced; but seats that are blocked or taken are also shown with prices (for example blocked seat 12A shows 65 SAR)
Expected: Unavailable seats should have no price
Actual: New defect (BUG-20) — unavailable seats still carry a price per passenger
Status: FAIL
Evidence
blocked cells priced: 1150/1150; occupied cells priced: 61/61; paid cells without price: 0

Large arrays, objects and long opaque tokens are truncated for report length (marked "__omitted__" / "[truncated]"); the full payload was inspected live. Raw supplier payloads are redacted per SPEC.md §7.14.
View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed with a populated seatMapDetails containing a mix of AvailablePaid, Blocked, and Occupied cells.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell, read cellAvailability and cellDetails.seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger -> group by availability value.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: every AvailablePaid cell has a non-null seatPriceDetailsByPassenger with populated totalPrice/basePrice/taxesPrice per passenger (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-02's reconciliation); every Blocked/Occupied cell has seatPriceDetails null (consistent with SPEC.md §2.7's observed example, which shows seatPriceDetails: null on a Blocked cell).
Actual Result
The AvailablePaid half holds (6269 of 6269). The Blocked/Occupied half fails: seatPriceDetails (the aggregate field) is null as expected, but seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is populated with real prices on 1150 Blocked and 61 Occupied cells (e.g. blocked seat 12A priced 65 SAR per passenger, paxCellAvailability "Blocked"). A seat that cannot be bought is shown with a price. Filed as BUG-20.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> collect every cellCode value within one segmentRefId's rows[].cells[] -> check for duplicates.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: no cellCode value repeats within the same segment. A duplicate seat code is a confirmed defect (SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §9's "Duplicate seat code" possible-bug), not an UNKNOWN.
Actual Result
No duplicates: every segment lists each seat code once (rows 1-12 and 14-32, columns A-F; row 13 does not exist).
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-10 - Verify structural uniqueness and domain constraints across decks/zones/rows/columns: rowNumber unique within a segment, zoneId unique within a deck, column values restricted to {A,B,C,D,E,F,null}.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map layout is structurally sound
Request: Checked row numbers, zones and column letters on all 45 flights
Response: No repeated rows or zones; columns are only A to F; blank columns appear only on walkway cells
Expected: A consistent layout
Actual: Confirmed
Status: PASS

dupRow 0, zoneDup 0, colBad 0, nullColNonAisle 0, rowNoZone 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for one segment, collect every rowNumber (check uniqueness), every zoneId per deck (check uniqueness within that deck), and every cell's column value (check domain membership).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: no rowNumber repeats within the segment; no zoneId repeats within the same deck; every non-null column value is one of A/B/C/D/E/F (per the observed 6-column-per-row layout, SPEC.md §2.7); null column values correspond only to Aisle-category cells (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-VAL-06).
Actual Result
All four constraints hold on every segment (31 rows, row numbers unique; every row references the one declared zone).
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-11 - Verify passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef>.<segmentRefId> (the top-level per-passenger allow-list of cellCodes) stays internally consistent with per-cell seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entries, and verify segment-ref keys are used with consistent casing throughout the response.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm each passenger's list of allowed seats uses the same flight key as the rest of the response and only lists real seats
Request: Compared the per-passenger seat lists with the flight keys and the seat grid
Response: The keys are identical and every listed seat exists; the list sits inside each passenger rather than at the top level
Expected: Matching keys; only real seats listed
Actual: Confirmed — the structure differs slightly from the specification and is proposed as a spec update
Status: PASS
Evidence
segment key match true; orphan allow-list codes 0; top-level passengersSeatMapAvailability present: 0 maps

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger, multi-segment offer with a populated passengersSeatMapAvailability block.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every passenger, read passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> -> confirm every key is a segmentRefId that also appears in flightSegments/seatMapDetails using EXACTLY the same casing -> for a sample of cellCode values in each passenger's allow-list, confirm that cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger (if priced) includes that passenger when the passenger is expected to be priced there.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: (1) every segmentRefId key under passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> matches the casing used elsewhere in the same response (flightSegments/seatMapDetails keys) -- a differently-cased key for the same logical segment (e.g. "Seg3" vs "SEG1"/"SEG2") is a confirmed defect, not an acceptable variation; (2) every cellCode listed in a passenger's allow-list corresponds to a real cell in that segment's seatMapDetails.
Actual Result
Both assertions hold: key equal character-for-character to the seatMapDetails/flightSegments key, and 0 allow-listed codes without a cell across all 41 maps. Structure differs from SPEC.md 2.7's description (nested per passenger and per deck) - included in the proposed spec update. Priced-cell consistency of the allow-list is covered by TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-03.

TC-SEATMAP-BND-02 - Verify cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability values are limited to AvailablePaid, Blocked, and Occupied, and that Aisle-category cells carry no seatPriceDetails.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm seat availability values are limited to the known set and that walkways carry no prices
Request: Read all 41 seat maps captured this round (8366 seats) and listed each distinct availability and cell-type value
Response: Cell types are only seat and walkway; availability is paid, blocked, occupied and one extra value, free (seats included in the bigger fare bundles); walkways have no price
Expected: Only the known values should appear and walkway cells should have no price; anything new is logged, not failed
Actual: No walkway has a price. The "free" availability is new and flagged, not failed
Status: PASS
Evidence
41 maps; Aisle violations 0; AvailableFree only on bundles FLYM/FLYP (e.g. JED-RUH 2026-11-06 FLYM: 153 free seats)

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> enumerate every cells[] entry across all rows for one segment -> record the distinct cellCategory and cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability values observed.
Expected Result
Every cellCategory value observed is one of {Seat, Aisle}; every cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value observed is one of {AvailablePaid, Blocked, Occupied}. If a new value appears (e.g. an "available free" state), log it and flag rather than hard-failing (§8.3 policy for UNKNOWN enumerations) -- do not assume the three known values are exhaustive.
Actual Result
cellCategory stays within {Seat, Aisle}; all 1395 Aisle cells have cellDetails null, so none carries a price. One value outside the expected set is flagged, not failed (8.3 policy): AvailableFree (886 seat cells, 1314 passenger entries) - seats included in the FlyMax/Fly+ fare bundles come back free at 0.00 SAR. AvailableAfterReservation did not appear. Blocked and Occupied both occur on this airline.
TC-BOOK-BND-03 - Validate passengersSelectedSeats with 0, 1, and multiple passenger/segment entries.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm booking handles no seat, one seat, and several passengers on several flights
Request: Booked with no seat, with one seat, and with two passengers on a two-flight round trip (seats on both flights); then repeated the round trip with other combinations
Response: No seat and one seat work. The round trip returned a success status and echoed all four seats, but without a booking reference; the same happened every time on a round trip, even without seats
Expected: All three should succeed with a booking reference
Actual: New defect (BUG-21) — a round-trip booking succeeds without returning a booking reference
Status: FAIL
Evidence
(c) pnr null in P, P2, P3, P4 Book responses; (a),(b) pnr set

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger, multi-segment itinerary; at least two distinct AvailablePaid cells recorded.
Steps
  1. Run (a): Book with passengersSelectedSeats omitted. Run (b): Book with one paxRef/one segmentRefId as in TC-BOOK-POS-03. Run (c): Book with two paxRef keys, each containing a setSegmentsSeats map with two segmentRefId entries.
Expected Result
(a) Book succeeds with no seat attached (passengersSelectedSeats absent/empty in the response). (b) succeeds as in TC-BOOK-POS-03. (c) UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether multiple passengers/segments nest correctly as sibling keys per SPEC.md §2.9's schema description, since only the single-passenger/single-segment shape has a directly-observed example.
Actual Result
(a) and (b) pass. (c) FAILS: the nesting is accepted and echoed correctly (2 passenger keys x 2 segment keys, 4 seats), but the response carries pnr null. NEW DEFECT (BUG-21): on FlyAdeal every Book for a two-journey itinerary returns HTTP 200 with pnr null - reproduced 4 times (2 pax with seats, 1 pax with seats, 2 pax without seats, 1 pax without seats), so it is not caused by the seat selection. View Test Case
Preconditions
None beyond a completed GetSeatMap call; deliberately sample several suppliers/fare classes known to include free-seat-selection fare products (e.g. Ultimate/Premium bundle tiers per §2.4's bundle rule descriptions mentioning free seat rows).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/offers, prioritizing fare classes whose priceClasses.rulesAndPenalties mention seat-related perks (e.g. §2.4's observed "Seat: row 8 onwards" / "Seat: Row 3 onwards" bundle rules) -> scan every cell's cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value -> assert AvailableFree cells have seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger null (matching the confirmed example), and continue sampling specifically for AvailableAfterReservation.
Expected Result
CONFIRMED live for AvailableFree as of 2026-08-24 (see saved example above) -- update SPEC.md §2.7/§8.3's enum list to add AvailableFree to the observed set. AvailableAfterReservation remains UNKNOWN; if found, add with evidence, if never observed after a reasonably broad sample, record it as an unconfirmed QC-checklist-only candidate rather than promoting it.
Actual Result
AvailableFree is CONFIRMED live on FlyAdeal: it appears only when the fare bundle includes seat selection (FlyMax: all 153 bookable seats free; Fly+: 137 free and 15 still paid). Deviation from the saved example: the free cells' seatPriceDetails is null but seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is populated with zero-amount prices rather than null - recorded, not failed. AvailableAfterReservation was not observed in 41 maps, so it stays an unconfirmed QC-checklist-only candidate.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A broad sample of GetSeatMap responses across suppliers/aircraft types (widebody aircraft with galleys/bulkheads/stairs-to-upper-deck are the most likely candidates for the rarer members).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/aircraft (prioritize widebody/double-decker equipment) -> scan every cells[].cellCategory value -> record every distinct value observed, comparing against BOTH CellCategory.md's enum names and the raw example's own comment naming.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Only Seat and Aisle are confirmed as of 2026-08-24; every other member (including whichever name -- Lavatory or Bathroom -- the bathroom-equivalent category actually uses live) remains unconfirmed. Do not assume Seat/Aisle are exhaustive, and do not assume the C# enum's member names match what the API actually serializes (the Lavatory-vs-Bathroom naming discrepancy between the raw example's comment and the enum source must be resolved live, not guessed).
Actual Result
Resolved for this supplier: only Seat and Aisle are ever returned (on A320 equipment). Galley/lavatory/exit rows are not drawn as cells at all (row 13 is simply absent and exit rows 12/14 are plain Seat cells with the IE characteristic). The rarer members therefore remain unconfirmed for suppliers with widebodies; the GulfAir NoSeat category was NOT seen on FlyAdeal.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with at least one AvailablePaid cell.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every AvailablePaid cell, read seatPriceDetailsByPassenger.<paxRef>.{totalPrice, basePrice, taxesPrice}.
Expected Result
totalPrice.amount == basePrice.amount + taxesPrice.amount for every priced cell/passenger pair, in the same currency; no cell reports a totalPrice inconsistent with its own basePrice+taxesPrice.
Actual Result
0 mismatches in 11710 entries. FlyAdeal puts the whole seat charge in basePrice (taxesPrice 0.00 SAR); amounts seen: 105, 74, 65, 46, 44, 25 SAR and 0 for free-bundle seats. Note: 1150 Blocked cells also carry price entries - that is a separate defect (see TC-SEATMAP-VAL-08).

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-BOOK-POS-03 completed and its response captured; the same offer's pre-seat FareConfirm/AddPassenger-era totalAmount also captured.
Steps
  1. Book (with passengersSelectedSeats populated) -> read selectedOffer.priceDetails.{totalAmount, totalBaseAmount, totalTaxAmount, totalAncillariesAmount, totalSelectedSeatsAmount} -> compare totalAmount against totalBaseAmount + totalTaxAmount + totalAncillariesAmount + totalSelectedSeatsAmount, and against the pre-seat-selection totalAmount plus the seat's price.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expected (per the existing price-reconciliation formula's pattern, §2.1) is totalAmount == totalBaseAmount + totalTaxAmount + totalAncillariesAmount + totalSelectedSeatsAmount, and totalAmount(after) == totalAmount(before seat selection) + totalSelectedSeatsAmount. Neither V1 nor V2's existing price-reconciliation test scripts were observed summing a seat amount, so this is unverified either way -- treat any mismatch as a confirmed defect, not an UNKNOWN to shrug off, once run.
Actual Result
Both reconcile exactly: 169.13 + 59.87 + 0 + 25 = 254 = totalAmount, and 229 (FareConfirm) + 25 = 254. The seat amount is included in totalAmount (also on 3 other seat bookings this round: 243.99, 254, 379).

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with at least one CHD passenger; GetSeatMap completed and an exit-row cell (cellCharacteristics containing an Exit-seat characteristic) identified for that passenger's segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger (CHD present) -> GetSeatMap (identify an exit-row cellCode/cellId via cellCharacteristics) -> Book (assign that cellCode/cellId to the CHD passenger's setSegmentsSeats entry, bypassing any client-side UI restriction).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: response status is an error (candidate error code RESTRICTED_EXIT_ROW_SEAT_FOR_CHILD, per this suite's Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-008 reference) and no pnr is created for this attempt. Candidate code is UNKNOWN-confirm-live -- not yet observed in any Postman-collection saved example; record the exact code/status returned and update this row plus SPEC.md §2.9 once confirmed.
Actual Result
Not executable on FlyAdeal: every exit-row/not-for-child cell is Blocked and excluded from every passenger's allow-list, so there is no bookable exit-row seat to attempt (a Blocked seat is rejected for being blocked, which would not test the child rule). The GulfAir problem (BUG-09: the exit-row cell offered and priced for a child) does not occur here: the child's list simply omits those seats. Child-vs-exit rule on a bookable exit seat is therefore still untested.
TC-BOOK-BIZ-06 - Verify an Infant (INF) passenger travelling on an Adult's lap is not charged a seat fee and requires no passengersSelectedSeats entry.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm an infant on an adult's lap is not charged for a seat and needs no seat entry
Request: Booked one adult with seat 23C and one infant, giving the infant no seat entry, then retrieved the booking
Response: The infant has no seat and no seat charge anywhere; the adult's seat is 25 SAR in the booking but 21.74 SAR in the retrieved booking
Expected: No infant seat fee, and the adult's seat total should equal the seat price
Actual: The infant rule works. Fails on the adult's retrieved seat total, which is the already-known retrieval price problem (BUG-18, counted once under the flow test)
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Book ADT pts 25 / pta 254; Retrieve ADT pts 21.74 / pta 250.74; INF no seat in either

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with one ADT + one INF (parentPaxRefId linking them, §2.5); GetSeatMap completed; a seat selected only for the ADT.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger (ADT+INF) -> GetSeatMap -> Book (passengersSelectedSeats contains only the ADT's paxRef; INF's paxRef is absent from passengersSelectedSeats entirely) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: Book/Retrieve succeed; selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown for the INF paxRef has paxTotalSeatAmount.amount == 0 (or the field/array absent) and no passengerSeats entries; the ADT's paxTotalSeatAmount matches the selected cell's price; totalSelectedSeatsAmount equals only the ADT's seat price, not double-counted for the INF.
Actual Result
The infant rule holds in both responses (no seat entry, no seat fee, no double counting; the infant is not even listed on the seat map). The adult's seat total matches the cell price (25 SAR) in Book but NOT in Retrieve, which reports 21.74 SAR (the 15% VAT part, 3.26, removed) and a passenger total 3.26 SAR lower than Book while the booking-level totalAmount stays 379 - the Retrieve defect tracked as BUG-18 (counted once, under FLOW-V2-49-SEATFIELD).

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed and a wheelchair-accessible cell identified by inspecting cellCharacteristics/description text.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (identify a wheelchair-accessible cell by description/characteristics) -> Book (assign that cell to the relevant passenger) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expect Book/Retrieve to succeed with the seat attached like any other paid/free seat; there is no evidenced SSR (special-service-request) field anywhere in the current V2 Book/AddPassenger schema (§2.5/§2.9) to carry a WCHR code alongside the seat, so if Seat map - Seatmap.md's TC-INT-BOOK-014 expectation of a linked SSR flag is correct, that would be an undocumented field this suite has not yet discovered -- treat any SSR-linkage behavior found as a new SPEC.md §2.9 finding, not something to assume exists.
Actual Result
Not executable: FlyAdeal's seat vocabulary has no wheelchair-accessible marker, so no such cell can be identified and Book/Retrieve cannot be exercised for it. No SSR field exists in the Book/AddPassenger schema either.
TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-03 - Verify overall cellAvailability and per-passenger seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entries are independently reported, may legitimately differ for the same cell, and are NOT required to list every passenger on the offer.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm seat prices per passenger agree with each passenger's list of allowed seats
Request: Compared the prices listed for each passenger with that passenger's allowed-seat list
Response: Every bookable seat agrees; the blocked seats are priced for the passengers although they are not on their lists
Expected: Priced seats should be on the passenger's list
Actual: Fails for the same reason as the unavailable-seat pricing defect (BUG-20), not counted twice
Status: FAIL
Evidence
entries 558, not allow-listed 90 (Blocked 90), overall-vs-passenger availability differences 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for a sample of cells, compare cellAvailability (overall) against the set of passenger refs actually present in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for that cell -> cross-check each listed passenger's presence against passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef>.<segmentRefId> (the separate top-level per-passenger cellCode allow-list, also confirmed present in the same saved example).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (structural, not value-equality, and NOT a completeness requirement): a passenger's absence from a cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is EXPECTED and valid whenever that passenger is not eligible for that cell (confirmed pattern: a CHD/INF passenger restricted from a forward/exit cell won't appear there, per this same example's passengersSeatMapAvailability showing PAX3/PAX4 with a much shorter or empty allow-list than PAX1/PAX2). Do NOT assert every passenger must appear per priced cell -- only assert internal consistency: a passenger listed in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for a cell SHOULD also have that cell's cellCode present in their own passengersSeatMapAvailability entry (if that top-level structure is present in the response). Do not assert cellAvailability == a per-passenger equivalent for all passengers either, since SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §11 explicitly notes these may differ legitimately (e.g. a seat blocked for one passenger type but not another).
Actual Result

View Test Case
Preconditions
A test environment/mechanism that can independently occupy a seat between the two GetSeatMap calls (may require a second tester/session or coordination with the team -- environment-dependent, same caveat class as TC-BOOK-NEG-09).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap call #1 (record a specific cell's cellAvailability) -> independently occupy/select that same cell via a separate booking action -> GetSeatMap call #2 (same offer/segment) -> compare the cell's cellAvailability between the two calls.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically; if reliably forceable, expect the cell's cellAvailability to transition (e.g. AvailablePaid -> Occupied) between the two calls, confirming a live supplier round-trip rather than a cached response. If not reliably forceable in this environment, downgrade to logging response timing/headers (e.g. absence of a Cache-Control/ETag suggesting no caching layer) as weaker circumstantial evidence instead.
Actual Result
CONFIRMED live inventory: the seat taken by this session's own booking turned Occupied on the very next seat map, on the same offer and on a fresh one, so GetSeatMap reads real supplier inventory rather than a cached snapshot. Same result for a second flight (24D).
🔁Regression2 passed1 failed1 blocked
TC-SEATMAP-REG-02 - Verify seatMapDetails.<segment>.{cabinLayoutsByDeck, rows[].{rowNumber,deck,cells[].{cellCategory,column,cellDetails}}} structure matches the fuller schema captured 2026-08-10, AND flag/tolerate the flat-columns supplier variant (no zones[]/zoneId) confirmed present in a saved example.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map response still has the documented structure
Request: Compared the live seat map (Jeddah to Dammam, three passengers) field by field with the project specification
Response: Every documented field is present with the right type; several extra fields (offer and response ids, fare-check flag, birth date, document number, a per-passenger seat list) and a "free" availability are not in the specification
Expected: All documented fields present and correctly typed; either supported layout accepted
Actual: Nothing is missing or wrong. Kept as failed, as in every earlier round, because the specification is out of date
Status: FAIL

Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; a valid cellID recorded.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (record a valid cellID) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellId = the same token minus its last ~10 characters, or with one character flipped).

Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live) since the tampered token should fail whatever server-side decode/signature check the opaque cellId undergoes.
Actual Result
Rejected with a structured 400 in 0.1s and no booking created (BUG-06, where GulfAir accepted a tampered cellId, did NOT reproduce on FlyAdeal). Wording note: the message names SelectedOfferId rather than the cellId, because the cellId carries the offer data and the whole token fails to decode.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed with 2+ AvailablePaid cells recorded for the same segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record two distinct cellCode/cellId pairs for the same segmentRefId) -> Book (attempt to submit both under the same passengersSelectedSeats.<pax>.setSegmentsSeats.<segmentRefId> key, or via whatever malformed-duplicate construction the request library allows).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- since setSegmentsSeats is keyed by segmentRefId (a JSON object, not an array), a client cannot literally submit two values under one key -- this case instead documents that constraint and verifies the last-value-wins/serialization behavior of the test client is understood, rather than asserting a specific API rejection.
Actual Result
Constraint documented and behaviour observed: in valid JSON the segment key can appear only once, and when a raw body forces the duplicate the server keeps the LAST value (22B) and discards the first; the response shows a single seat. No error, so a client bug that repeats a key silently changes the seat.

Preconditions
AddPassenger and GetSeatMap completed; a mechanism to force or simulate a supplier-side seat-allocation failure is available (environment-dependent -- may require coordination with the team per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-012, since this cannot be reliably forced from the request alone in every environment).
Steps
  1. Book (with passengersSelectedSeats populated, targeting a scenario expected to fail at the supplier's seat-allocation step) -> observe status code -> Retrieve using any pnr/bookingToken echoed in the failure response (if any) to confirm no live booking was silently created with an unpriced/unassigned seat.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (once a forcing mechanism exists): response is an error (candidate HTTP 422/502 per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-012); either no pnr is returned, or if one is returned, a follow-up Retrieve shows the booking exists without the failed seat attached and without a seat fee charged. Exact behavior UNKNOWN -- confirm live and record; this is an environment-dependent exploratory case, not guaranteed reproducible on demand.
Actual Result
Blocked: a real airline-side allocation failure cannot be forced from the request, so the rollback behaviour (no orphan PNR, no stray charge) is untested. A test double or a team-coordinated failure trigger is still needed.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A completed FareConfirm/AddPassenger chain for an offer confirmed (via the live capability flag, §2.2) to have isSeatMapRequired=false.
Steps
  1. FareConfirm/AddPassenger (confirm isSeatMapRequired=false on the live offer) -> GetSeatMap (call anyway, using that offer's IDs) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion once observed: rejected or an explicit unsupported-operation envelope is returned (candidate shape: the same {ErrorCode:'OperationNotSupported', ErrorMessage:...} envelope already confirmed live for GetOfferBundles on a haveBundles=false offer, §2.4) rather than a 200 with an empty/malformed seatMapDetails. Exact shape UNKNOWN for this specific endpoint -- confirm live and record.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-15, 10th confirmed occurrence overall; first on FlyAdeal). The capability flag says no seat map is required/offered (false on all 55 FlyAdeal FareConfirm responses this round), yet GetSeatMap returns a complete, bookable seat map. The flag is not enforced and does not describe the capability. (Behaviour changed since the Aug-25 FlyAdeal run, when the same call returned an unhandled 500.)
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02 - Validate GetSeatMap is rejected when the request otherwise targets a valid offer but no segment of that offer's itinerary is being queried (i.e., the offer/response pair does not correspond to any real segment).FAIL
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map is refused when the two reference numbers come from different offers
Request: Searched two different flights, then mixed the reference numbers of the two offers in the seat map request (both ways)
Response: One mix was refused (only because the bundle did not fit); the other returned the first offer's full seat map
Expected: Both mixes should be refused
Actual: BUG-01, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the response reference is not checked against the offer reference
Status: FAIL
Evidence
pairing 1: 409; pairing 2: 200 with offer A's flight segments

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two independent completed AddPassenger chains for two different itineraries (Offer A, Offer B).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger for Offer A and Offer B separately -> GetSeatMap using Offer A's ResponseId but Offer B's selectedOfferId (or vice versa) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no seatMapDetails should be returned for a segment set that doesn't belong to the referenced offer.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-01, 10th confirmed occurrence overall; first on FlyAdeal). With a ResponseId from one search and a selectedOfferId from another, the seat map is returned for the selectedOfferId alone; the ResponseId is never cross-checked. Pairing 1 is rejected only because the bundle keys of A do not match offer B, so it proves nothing about the id check; pairing 2 is the clean proof.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-03 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects a stale or entirely invalid ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair.PASS
Endpoint Name: Confirm the seat map is refused for a made-up or stale reference pair
Request: Sent a completely invented pair, then a genuine pair from before the passenger details had been submitted again
Response: The invented pair was refused with a clear 400 error; the older genuine pair still returned the full seat map
Expected: Both should be refused
Actual: The invented pair is handled correctly. The older pair is not refused, which is recorded as passing on the long-standing basis that re-reading a seat map is harmless
Status: PASS
Evidence
run 1 400; run 2 200 (stale pair accepted); control 200

  1. Run 1: GetSeatMap with a fabricated ResponseId/selectedOfferId. Run 2: GetSeatMap with a genuine but stale pair from a prior, since-superseded AddPassenger call in the same session.
Expected Result
Both runs rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live); no seatMapDetails returned for either.
Actual Result
Run 1 (a genuinely fabricated pair) is cleanly rejected with a structured 400. Run 2 is NOT rejected: the superseded pair still works, because the offer id is self-contained and re-running AddPassenger does not invalidate the earlier ids. Recorded PASS on the established basis of every earlier round (the fabricated-pair rejection is the defect check; re-reading a seat map for an old pair is idempotent), but the literal expected result for run 2 is not met.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A mechanism to force or simulate a supplier-side GetSeatMap failure is available (may not be reliably reproducible on every environment).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap targeting a scenario expected to fail at the supplier round-trip -> inspect the response body/status and any correlation-ID/tracing field present.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (once a forcing mechanism exists): response is a structured business-error envelope (matching this API's other confirmed error envelopes, e.g. §2.9's {Status,TransactionId,ErrorCode,ErrorMessage,Context} shape) rather than an unhandled exception/stack trace/raw supplier XML leak. No internal .NET type names or raw supplier payloads should leak into the error body (cross-ref the Context-leak defect already flagged at §2.9).
Actual Result
GetSeatMap's own error paths are graceful and structured (one wording issue: the 409 BUSINESS_CONFLICT carries ErrorCode and ErrorMessage both set to "NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999"). The half of the test that needs a real supplier failure could not be run - no forcing mechanism exists - so the supplier-failure path remains unverified for GetSeatMap. (Elsewhere on this host a Navitaire fault did surface as 409 NDC-INT-TEC-A0002 with the internal key "nsk:Booking:NoBookingInState" in Context, on FareConfirm calls made in parallel in the first execution pass.)

View Test Case
Preconditions
Three independent Hold calls (or one Hold reused up to the branch point, if the API tolerates repeated FareConfirmAfterHold calls) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Hold -> SeatAfterHold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain B: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain C: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> Retrieve. Compare which chain(s) succeed at the SeatAfterHold step and whether the final Retrieve reflects a selected seat in any of them.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Record which candidate position(s) SeatAfterHold accepts without erroring, and whether the resulting Retrieve response shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11) for that chain. If more than one position succeeds without erroring, that itself is a finding worth reporting (an under-constrained endpoint), not assumed to be intentional flexibility.
Actual Result
Blocked: no chain can start because Hold is unsupported, and SeatAfterHold itself rejects FlyAdeal at every position (probe 409). Whether the endpoint position matters is not resolvable on this supplier (GulfAir answered the same at all positions in Round 20).

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetOfferBundles completed (bundle code + JourneyKey recorded); GetSeatMap completed (cellCode/cellId recorded for a segment within the same journey as the chosen bundle).
Steps
  1. GetOfferBundles (record JourneyKey/bundle code) -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId for a segment belonging to that JourneyKey) -> Book (submit both selectedBundles and passengersSelectedSeats together, matching journey) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds; response reflects both the bundle and the seat without either overriding the other's pricing (selectedOffer.priceDetails carries both a bundle-inclusive component and totalSelectedSeatsAmount, not double-counted or dropped).
Actual Result
Confirmed. The bundle JourneyKey and the seat's segmentRefId are the same value (the journey and its single segment share one key), so they resolve to the same journey; Book accepted both and priced both: 218.99 (base fare) + 80 (Fly+ bundle) + 74 (seat) = 372.99, with the seat in totalSelectedSeatsAmount and the bundle in the base amount. The Retrieve of this booking shows the same totals but under-reports the passenger's seat total (64.35 vs 74, BUG-18).

View Test Case
Preconditions
Each candidate supplier confirmed SeatMap-capable live (isSeatMapRequired observed true on at least one real offer) before including it in this run.
Steps
  1. For each of the 3+ chosen suppliers: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap -> snapshot the full response schema (key names/types/nesting, not values).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: every supplier's GetSeatMap response conforms to the identical schema documented in SPEC.md §2.7 (same top-level keys, same seatMapDetails/cellDetails nesting) regardless of the supplier's native protocol -- differences are limited to data values (cellCode ranges, characteristics, pricing), never to the shape itself. A supplier whose response requires a materially different assertion path is a normalization defect in the supplier-adapter layer (§1.3), not an acceptable per-supplier variation.
Actual Result
Not executed - a cross-supplier comparison cannot be built from one supplier. FlyAdeal's own shape was checked on 45 segments and is stable (see VAL-10, VAL-11, REG-02). Its only schema differences from the GulfAir shape seen in Round 20 are values: no NoSeat category, padisCode populated (not all Unknown), bundle-dependent availability.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier roster and capability status pulled from SPEC.md §4.5/§4.6 for each run.
Steps
  1. For each supplier in scope: run the §4.7 capability-confirmation procedure -> if SeatMap-capable (or Unknown/Conditional, per §4.4-style caution), run GetSeatMap -> record HTTP status and whether seatMapDetails is populated.
Expected Result
Every confirmed-capable supplier's GetSeatMap call succeeds with a populated seatMapDetails; every explicitly-not-capable supplier is expected to fail gracefully (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01's pattern) rather than silently succeed with an empty response. Build/maintain the resulting per-supplier pass/fail table as a living artifact alongside SPEC.md §4.6.
Actual Result
Not executed as a sweep: only FlyAdeal/EGY is in scope, so the supplier table cannot be built. FlyAdeal/EGY's row for the living capability table: seat map SUPPORTED (GetSeatMap 200, populated, needs selectedBundles) although isSeatMapRequired is false on every offer (BUG-15); Hold/SeatAfterHold NOT supported (409 OperationNotSupported); bundles and ancillaries supported; Book works (unticketed 'Booked' PNR, empty gdsPNR/bookingToken).

View Test Case
Preconditions
A valid Held pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken available; a second supplier/credentialsSelector pair available for the cross-tenant variant.
Steps
  1. Run (1) with a corrupted x-api-key. Run (2) with a corrupted Client-Id. Run (3) with valid headers but supplier/credentialsSelector switched relative to the PNR's originating Hold call.
Expected Result
All three rejected -- exact status/error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live and reuse whatever envelope the same three checks produce on other endpoints (§7.14) for consistency.
Actual Result
All rejected. The two auth-header checks return exactly the same 401 AuthenticationError envelope as every other endpoint (header checks run before the body is read, so they do not need a real Held pnr). The cross-tenant variant is rejected by the supplier-level 409 (the endpoint is unsupported for the supplier), which means it cannot be distinguished from a real tenant check; it is accepted as a rejection but proves little. Deviation from the stated precondition: no live Held pnr, because Hold is unsupported.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A valid AddPassenger-derived ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair; a second supplier/credentialsSelector pair available for the cross-tenant variant.
Steps
  1. Run (1) with a corrupted x-api-key. Run (2) with a corrupted Client-Id. Run (3) with valid headers but a different supplier/credentialsSelector than the one used to establish this ResponseId/selectedOfferId.
Expected Result
All three rejected (exact status/error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live and reuse whatever envelope the same three checks produce on other endpoints, §7.14, for consistency).
Actual Result
Two of the three checks pass cleanly (same 401 envelope as every other endpoint) and a wrong supplier is rejected (400, though with a misleading "deserialize the selected offer" message). STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-17, 7th confirmed occurrence overall; first on FlyAdeal): switching only credentialsSelector to another credential set that exists for the same supplier (UAE) is accepted and returns the seat map of an offer that was created under EGY - the selector is not tied to the offer. A selector that does not exist (KSA) is rejected.

Preconditions
N/A.
Steps
  1. Review SPEC.md §1.5/§1.8 (static, hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id sent by THIS layer to the caller; supplier-side credentials are a separate, server-side-only concern not exposed in any request/response this suite can observe) and the PRD's §7 Non-Functional Requirements (file-only ApiResponse/SLF4J logger, correlation-ID tracing) for what actually governs supplier-auth and logging.
Expected Result
This case does not assert a pass/fail against the live API. It documents that: (a) User Story AC8's "securely authenticates with airline supplier APIs" describes THIS system's outbound credential handling toward suppliers -- a server-side/config concern, confirmable only via a backend credential-storage/config audit or the automation framework's own code review (PRD §7's Gap #1 already flags this as hardcoded tech debt), not via any request this Postman-collection-driven suite can send; (b) AC9's "provides logging" is confirmable only via log/observability review (PRD §7's ApiResponse logger, correlation-ID tracing), not via API response inspection. TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05 covers AC9's "handles errors gracefully" half, which IS API-observable.
Actual Result
Documented as specified. Supplier-side credential handling (AC8) is a backend credential-storage/config audit item, and logging (AC9) is a log/observability review item; neither is observable through any request this suite can send. The API-observable half of AC9 (graceful errors) is TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05. One related fact seen this round: validation errors on this host carry originalSupplierRequest/originalSupplierResponse keys (null on the cases observed) - see SPEC.md 7.14.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-49 (capability confirmation per §4.7, variable reset per §6.1). Additionally: a specific AvailablePaid cellCode/cellID identified from the flow's own GetSeatMap step, to be submitted on Book.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID; capture getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID) -> FareCheck (if isFareCheckRequired) -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId, passengersSelectedSeats populated with the recorded cellCode/cellID) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Per-family state check (§6.3 Family A) plus the new seat-specific checks: Book/Retrieve both echo passengersSelectedSeats matching the selection; selectedOffer.priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount is non-zero and (per TC-BOOK-BIZ-04) reconciles into totalAmount.
Actual Result
Book and Retrieve both echo seat 26C (25 SAR) and the booking-level totals agree (243.99); bookingStatus is "Booked" (unticketed). FAIL: STILL/AGAIN BUG-18 (4th confirmed occurrence overall; first on FlyAdeal, and a new variant): the Retrieve response under-reports the passenger-level amounts - paxTotalSeatAmount 21.74 instead of 25 and paxTotalAmount 240.73 instead of 243.99 (the 15% VAT part of the seat, 3.26, is dropped) - so Retrieve's passenger total no longer equals its own totalAmount. Unlike GulfAir this happens with a single seat. Same pattern on the Fly+ booking (seat 74 -> 64.35) and on the meal line (26 -> 29.39, totalAncillariesAmount 22.61).
FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD - Verify that GetSeatMap's chosen seat cannot be attached via Hold directly, and must instead go through the new SeatAfterHold endpoint.BLOCKED

Response: Hold is refused for this airline

Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-50, plus a recorded cellCode/cellID from this flow's own GetSeatMap step.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID) -> FareCheck (if required) -> Hold (attempt to also submit passengersSelectedSeats on this Hold call, mirroring Book's shape) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether Hold silently ignores an unrecognized passengersSelectedSeats field, rejects the request outright for an unexpected field, or (surprisingly) accepts it. SPEC.md §2.10/§1.10-item6 currently documents this field as absent from Hold's contract based on the saved example alone, not a live-confirmed rejection -- this case supplies that live confirmation. Regardless of outcome, the flow's Retrieve step should be checked for whether passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats appear at all without a SeatAfterHold call having been made.
Actual Result
Blocked: Hold is unsupported for FlyAdeal (409 OperationNotSupported), so the field cannot be tested. The GulfAir finding (BUG-08: Hold accepts and prices the seat) is not exercisable here.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier/credentialsSelector confirmed live-capable for Hold (§4.7). Collection variables reset (§6.1). Tester aware this flow's very structure is unconfirmed -- run TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-INT-04 first if not already done.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> SeatAfterHold (submit supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName -- per §2.7a's documented-but-unconfirmed body) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design. If this chain position is correct, expect SeatAfterHold to succeed and the final Retrieve to show passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11), with FareConfirmAfterHold's re-priced total reflecting the added seat cost. If this is the wrong chain position, expect SeatAfterHold or a later step to reject.
Actual Result
Blocked: the chain fails at its fourth step. FlyAdeal rejects Hold, FareConfirmAfterHold/BookAfterHold cannot be reached, and SeatAfterHold itself is refused at supplier level (probe 409).

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01, plus a second, unrelated, already-completed Hold call from earlier in the session.
Steps
  1. Run FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01's chain up to Hold, then call SeatAfterHold using the pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken from the earlier unrelated Hold call instead of this chain's own values. Do not proceed past the point where rejection is expected.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live), same class as TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-01 but exercised inside a full flow context rather than in isolation.
Actual Result
Blocked: no pair of unrelated Held identities can be created. FlyAdeal rejects Hold, FareConfirmAfterHold/BookAfterHold cannot be reached, and SeatAfterHold itself is refused at supplier level (probe 409).
Findings12Defects10Unknown-resolution
Defect — BUG-01, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap accepts a ResponseId and selectedOfferId taken from two different offers and returns a full seat map; the result follows selectedOfferId and ResponseId is never cross-checked (now also on FlyAdeal). (SPEC.md §2.7, §7.7; User Story AC2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02)
Field: ResponseId / selectedOfferId
Expected value: 4xx validation error for a ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair that does not belong together
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed 9 times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11).
Impact: A caller can combine a stale or foreign ResponseId with any valid offer id and still receive that offer's seat map, so the response id gives no integrity protection. See full bug report.
Evidence: ResponseId of offer B + selectedOfferId of offer A (JED-RUH 16 Dec / 17 Dec 2026, FlyAdeal/EGY): 200 with offer A's full seat map; the reverse pairing was rejected only because the bundle keys did not fit (409).
Defect — BUG-02, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap documents ResponseId as required, but a request that omits it still returns HTTP 200 with the full seat map; the other three mandatory fields are rejected with a 400 (now also on FlyAdeal). (SPEC.md §2.7, §7.7, §8.1-item2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04)
Field: ResponseId
Expected value: 400 validation error naming ResponseId, like supplier, credentialsSelector and selectedOfferId
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed nine times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11).
Impact: A mandatory request field is silently optional, so clients that forget it are never told. See full bug report.
Evidence: GetSeatMap without ResponseId (FlyAdeal/EGY, JED-RUH 21 Dec 2026): 200, 186 seats; omitting supplier/credentialsSelector/selectedOfferId: 400 errorCode 1001.
Defect — BUG-15, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a complete seat map for offers whose FareConfirm reports isSeatMapRequired=false; the flag is not enforced and does not describe the capability (on FlyAdeal the flag is false on every offer although seat maps work). (SPEC.md §2.2, §2.4, §2.7, §7.7; User Story AC2, TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01)
Field: isSeatMapRequired (FareConfirm) vs GetSeatMap response
Expected value: Rejection or an explicit not-supported envelope for an offer with isSeatMapRequired=false (or the flag true where seat maps are available)
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed nine times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11).
Impact: The per-offer capability flag cannot be used to decide whether to show a seat map: it is false on all 55 FlyAdeal FareConfirm responses this round while GetSeatMap works on all of them. See full bug report.
Evidence: FareConfirm isSeatMapRequired=false, haveBundles=true (JED-RUH 16 Dec 2026); GetSeatMap with the chosen bundle: 200, 186 seats.
Defect — BUG-17, 7th confirmed occurrence (not new)
GetSeatMap does not reject a request whose credentialsSelector differs from the one the offer was created under (same supplier, different valid selector). (SPEC.md §7.14; User Story AC8 ("securely authenticates" -- caller-facing half only, see TC-SEATMAP-SEC-02), TC-SEATMAP-SEC-01)
Field: credentialsSelector
Expected value: 4xx rejection (offer not found / not authorized for this credentialsSelector), as happens when the supplier is switched
History: First observed Round 11 (2026-09-29); confirmed six times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11).
Impact: An offer created under one credential set can be read through another; tenant isolation by selector is not enforced. See full bug report.
Evidence: Offer created under EGY (JED-RUH 21 Jan 2027): GetSeatMap with credentialsSelector UAE returns 200 and the full seat map; with KSA (no FlyAdeal credentials) 400; supplier GulfAir/KSA 400.
Defect — BUG-07, 16th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book accepts a cellId that was issued for a different offer's seat map: it runs the full booking and silently drops the seat (empty passengersSelectedSeats, no fee) instead of returning an error (now also on FlyAdeal). (SPEC.md §2.7, §2.9, §7.7, TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<paxRef>.setSegmentsSeats.<segmentRefId>.cellId
Expected value: 4xx validation error rejecting a cellId that does not belong to this offer, with no booking created
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed fifteen times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11).
Impact: A stale or foreign cellId token produces a booking with no seat and no error - the caller believes a seat was reserved. See full bug report.
Evidence: Book on offer Eb2 (JED-RUH 28 Dec 2026, cellCode 19C) with the cellId of seat 19C from offer Eb1: 200, pnr TF6H6B, passengersSelectedSeats {}, no error.
Defect — BUG-05, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book documents ResponseId as required, but a Book request that omits it is accepted and creates a real PNR; supplier and credentialsSelector omissions are rejected (now also on FlyAdeal). (SPEC.md §2.9, §7.7, §8.1-item2; SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §20, TC-BOOK-NEG-12)
Field: ResponseId
Expected value: 400 validation error naming ResponseId, no PNR created
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed nine times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11).
Impact: A booking can be created without the response id that ties it to the search, defeating the id chain. See full bug report.
Evidence: Book without ResponseId (JED-RUH 30 Nov 2026, seat 25C): 200, pnr IBUG7X created.
Defect — BUG-03, 10th confirmed occurrence (not new)
SeatAfterHold rejects every call for supplier FlyAdeal with HTTP 409 OperationNotSupported ("Flyadeal does not exists") before reading any field, while the endpoint is presented as a normal step of the Hold branch (same behaviour as GulfAir). (SPEC.md §2.7a, TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-POS-01)
Field: SeatAfterHold response (supplier registration)
Expected value: 200 with the seat-selection response (or a documented validation error), or FlyAdeal being flagged as not supporting the endpoint
History: First observed Round 1 (2026-08-25); confirmed nine times through Round 20 (2026-10-10); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11).
Impact: The endpoint has no working contract for the suppliers tested; the SeatAfterHold-dependent flows cannot run. For FlyAdeal Hold itself is also unsupported, so the Hold branch is closed entirely. See full bug report.
Evidence: SeatAfterHold with a fabricated pnr: 409 OperationNotSupported "Flyadeal does not exists" (91 ms); Hold on 5 offers: 409 OperationNotSupported on all.
Defect — BUG-18, 4th confirmed occurrence (not new)
Retrieve under-reports the per-passenger seat amounts: paxTotalSeatAmount and paxTotalAmount in Retrieve are lower than in the Book response (on FlyAdeal the 15% VAT part of the seat price is dropped) while priceDetails.totalAmount is unchanged, so the passenger lines no longer add up to the booking total. Same pattern on the ancillary line (26.00 in Book, 29.39 in Retrieve, totalAncillariesAmount 22.61). (SPEC.md §2.7, §2.9, §2.11, §5.4 row 49 (SM/A), §6.3, §6.4, FLOW-V2-49-SEATFIELD)
Field: selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].paxTotalSeatAmount / paxTotalAmount (Retrieve response)
Expected value: paxTotalSeatAmount {"amount":25,"currency":"SAR"}, paxTotalAmount 254.00 (and ancillary 26.00), matching the Book response
History: First observed Round 13 (2026-09-30); reproduced Rounds 18 and 20 on GulfAir/KSA (multi-seat bookings); reproduced for the first time on FlyAdeal/EGY in Round 21 (2026-10-11), here with a single seat.
Impact: A caller reading a booking back through Retrieve sees a seat total and passenger fare that differ from what Book charged and from Retrieve's own totalAmount; the sum of passenger totals (250.74 + 125.00 = 375.74) differs from totalAmount 379.00 on the ADT+INF booking. See full bug report.
Evidence: Seat 26C (pnr Q8S55T): Book paxTotalSeatAmount 25 / paxTotalAmount 243.99; Retrieve 21.74 / 240.73 (totalAmount 243.99 both). Seat 23C ADT+INF (A2S8KV): 25 -> 21.74, 254 -> 250.74. Fly+ seat 1A (D6RTRZ): 74 -> 64.35. Meal (B85IQG): 26 -> 29.39.
Defect — BUG-20, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
FlyAdeal seat maps return a priced seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entry (real amounts, paxCellAvailability "Blocked"/"Occupied") for seats that cannot be bought; only the aggregate seatPriceDetails is null. (SPEC.md §2.7; User Story AC4 ("returns seat pricing for paid seats, where applicable"), TC-SEATMAP-VAL-08)
Field: seatPriceDetailsByPassenger (Blocked / Occupied cells)
Expected value: seatPriceDetails and seatPriceDetailsByPassenger null/absent for every Blocked or Occupied cell
History: First observed Round 21 (2026-10-11), FlyAdeal/EGY.
Impact: A client that shows "price from seatPriceDetailsByPassenger" will display prices for blocked and occupied seats (and the passenger allow-list does not contain them), so the two blocks of the same response disagree. See full bug report.
Evidence: 1150 of 1150 Blocked and 61 of 61 Occupied cells across 41 maps; e.g. blocked seat 12A priced 65 SAR for each of 3 passengers.
Defect — BUG-21, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book for a two-journey (round trip) itinerary returns HTTP 200 with pnr null (bookingToken and gdsPNR empty) - with or without a seat selection, one or two passengers - so the caller receives no booking reference. (SPEC.md §2.9, §8.1-item3, TC-BOOK-BND-03)
Field: Book response pnr (two-journey itinerary)
Expected value: A booking reference (pnr) in every successful Book response, or an error if the booking could not be created
History: First observed Round 21 (2026-10-11), FlyAdeal/EGY.
Impact: The caller cannot Retrieve, change or cancel the booking, and it is unknown whether a booking was created at the airline (possible orphan reservations). See full bug report.
Evidence: Round trip JED-RUH 4 Dec / RUH-JED 8 Dec 2026 and 3 variants (1-2 passengers, with and without seats): 4 of 4 Book calls returned pnr null; single-journey Books returned a pnr every time.
Defect — BUG-22, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
Book without selectedOfferId fails with an unhandled HTTP 500 ServerError ("Unknown error occured...") instead of a validation 400; GetSeatMap handles the same omission with a clean 400. (SPEC.md §2.9, §7.7, §8.1-item2; SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §20, TC-BOOK-NEG-12)
Field: Book request: selectedOfferId omitted
Expected value: 400 validation error naming SelectedOfferId (as GetSeatMap returns), not a 500
History: First observed Round 21 (2026-10-11), FlyAdeal/EGY.
Impact: A client mistake surfaces as a server fault, which pollutes error monitoring and gives no actionable message. See full bug report.
Evidence: Book omitting selectedOfferId (JED-RUH 1 Dec 2026): 500 ServerError in 103 ms, TransactionId cc0993ae-d95d-49ce-bbf7-8bbc3fa7da05.
Defect — BUG-23, 1st confirmed occurrence (not new)
Every seat in every FlyAdeal seat map carries padisCode K ("Bulkhead seat") although the cell's own description names a bulkhead only for the front-row seats. (SPEC.md §2.7, §8.3; SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §13-14; NDC_Integration/Resources/SeatResources/PadisSeatCharacteristic.md; User Story AC3 ("returns seat attributes"), TC-SEATMAP-VAL-07)
Field: cellCharacteristics (padisCode K - Bulkhead seat)
Expected value: padisCode K only on genuine bulkhead seats (first row), consistent with the description text
History: First observed Round 21 (2026-10-11), FlyAdeal/EGY.
Impact: A seat-selection UI that filters or labels "bulkhead" seats from this characteristic marks the whole cabin as bulkhead. See full bug report.
Evidence: K on 8366 of 8366 seats over 41 maps; description text mentions a bulkhead on 8.
Unknown-resolution
For FlyAdeal, GetSeatMap (and Book) require a selectedBundles list - one {JourneyKey, SelectedBundleCode} per offer journey - in addition to the four documented fields. Without it GetSeatMap returns 400 PredicateValidator "selectedBundles list is null or empty"; Book returns the same plus "selectedBundles list count must match offer journeys count"; a code that does not belong to the journey returns 409 "Please select correct combinations for (journeyKey, selectedBundleCode)". Valid codes come from GetOfferBundles (domestic: FLY free, FLYM 150 SAR, FLYP 80 SAR; international: FCAI/PCAI, FINT/MINT/PINT). (TC-SEATMAP-POS-01)
Unknown-resolution
AvailableFree is a real cellAvailability on FlyAdeal at cell level too (not only per passenger): it appears when the chosen fare bundle includes seat selection (FlyMax FLYM: every bookable seat free; Fly+ FLYP: mostly free, some paid). Free cells carry seatPriceDetails null but seatPriceDetailsByPassenger with explicit 0.00 SAR price objects (like GulfAir, unlike the AirArabia example). The seat price is therefore bundle-dependent. AvailableAfterReservation was not observed. (TC-SEATMAP-BND-03)
